# Introduction

Hierarchical time series are time series that can be divided into sub-series with different levels of aggregation. In `persephone3`, such objects are created similar to a nested list structure.

The following example creates a hierarchical object with two subseries `a` and `b`:

```{r}
library(persephone3)

hts <- perHts(
  a = perX13(AirPassengers),
  b = perTramo(AirPassengers)
)
hts
```

## Running the Model

When the `run()` method of `hts` is invoked, the following adjustments are performed:

1. The aggregate series `a+b` is adjusted and the results are saved in `hts$output`
2. `a` is adjusted using X-13ARIMA-SEATS
3. `b` is adjusted using TRAMO/SEATS

The results can be viewed as follows:

```{r}
display_result <- function(ts) {
  window(ts, end = c(1949, 6))
}

hts$run()

# Direct adjustment (seasonally adjusted aggregate series)
display_result(hts$adjusted)

# Seasonally adjusted component series "a"
display_result(hts$components$a$adjusted)

# Indirect adjustment (sum of seasonally adjusted components)
display_result(hts$adjustedIndirect)
```

The last line displays the results of an indirect adjustment, which amounts to `a$adjusted` + `b$adjusted` in this case.

## Multiple Levels of Hierarchies

For more complex structures with multiple hierarchy levels, `perHts` calls can be nested:

```{r}
hts_nested <- perHts(
  hts = hts,
  hts_child = perHts(
    a = perX13(AirPassengers)
  ),
  b = perTramo(AirPassengers)
)

hts_nested
```

As you can see, the structure of `hts` is available within this nested object.

## Several Aggregates with `groups`

If there are many aggregates and sub-aggregates, `perHts()` can also be used
with a flat structure: all series (the sub-series *and* the aggregates) are
supplied at one level and `groups` describes which series build which
aggregate. Every series is adjusted exactly once, no matter how many
aggregates it belongs to, and each aggregate has its own weights. Aggregates
are always built from their leaf series, so a sub-aggregate listed as a
sub-series of another aggregate is replaced by its own sub-series:

```{r}
groups <- list(
  ab = c("a", "b"),
  bc = c("b", "c"),
  all = c("a", "b", "c")
)
```

Here `a`, `b` and `c` are the leaves; `ab`, `bc` and `all` are the aggregates,
each with its own weights. The aggregate series themselves have to be supplied
as series as well, since they are needed for the direct adjustment and for
their chain linking factors.

## Indirect Adjustment of Chain Linked Series

For chain linked series the indirect adjustment cannot be obtained by summing
up the adjusted sub-series: the chain linking factors of the sub-series do not
give the factor of the aggregate. Instead, the adjustment is performed in the
unchained space:

1. the sub-series are adjusted as usual,
2. they are unchained by their chain linking factors,
3. the unchained adjusted series are weighted together,
4. the result is chain linked again with the factor of the aggregate,
5. and finally re-referenced to a base year (`ref_year`).

The following (simulated) example adjusts the chain linked series `a`, `b` and
`c` and builds the indirectly adjusted aggregate `all` from them; the factors
are the levels of the chain linking, i.e. the chain linked series is the
unchained series multiplied by its factor:

```{r}
n <- 12 * 20
tt <- seq_len(n)
ul <- list(                       # the unchained levels
  a = 100 + 0.5 * tt + 5 * sin(2 * pi * tt / 12),
  b = 60 + 0.3 * tt + 3 * sin(2 * pi * tt / 12 + 1),
  c = 40 + 0.2 * tt + 2 * sin(2 * pi * tt / 12 + 2)
)
lf <- list(                       # the chain linking factors
  a = 0.5 + 0.002 * tt, b = 0.6 + 0.001 * tt, c = 0.55 + 0.0015 * tt
)
w <- c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2)
ul_all <- Reduce("+", Map("*", ul, as.list(w)))
lf_all <- Reduce("+", Map(function(u, l, wi) u * l * wi, ul, lf, as.list(w))) /
  ul_all                          # factor of the aggregate

series <- c(Map("*", ul, lf), list(all = ul_all * lf_all))
mts <- ts(do.call("cbind", series), start = c(2000, 1), frequency = 12)
lfm <- ts(cbind(do.call("cbind", lf), all = lf_all),
          start = c(2000, 1), frequency = 12)

hts_cl <- perHts(
  list = mts, method = "x13", template = "rsa0",
  groups = list(all = c("a", "b", "c")), weights = list(all = w),
  cl_weights = lfm, ref_year = 2010,
  adjustment = "indirect"         # the aggregate is not adjusted itself
)
hts_cl$run()

# the indirectly adjusted aggregate (re-referenced to 2010 = 100)
window(hts_cl$getAdjustedIndirect("all"), start = c(2010, 1), end = c(2010, 6))
```

With `adjustment = "both"` the aggregates are adjusted directly as well and
both results are available (`$getAdjustedDirect()` and
`$getAdjustedIndirect()`); with `adjustment = "direct"` only the direct
adjustment is computed. `$getUnchainedIndirect()` returns the aggregate of
step 3, before it is chain linked again. Trading day regressors for the
individual series are given with `td`, either one regressor set for all
series or a named list with one entry per series, e.g.
`td = list(a = td_a, c = td_c)`. The further user-defined regressors of the
regression model (no trading days, e.g. the centered leap year regressor
`genTd()[[3]][, "lpYear", drop = FALSE]`) are given with `user` in the same
way; without `groups` a single set of regressors is also used for the aggregate
series itself, which is adjusted on its own there. The regressors of one series
are shown by the `summary()` of that series, e.g.
`summary(hts$components$a)`.

## Iterating Over the Hierarchy Tree

To iterate over all components of a `perHts` object, the `iterate()` method can be used. It behaves similarly to `lapply()` and allows you to apply custom functions to each node in the hierarchy:

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Run the model first
hts_nested$run()

# Apply custom function to get mean and standard deviation
hts_nested$iterate(asTable = TRUE, function(obj) {
  list(
    mean = mean(obj$adjusted),
    sd = sd(obj$adjusted)
  )
})
```

## Setting Options Recursively

When creating a `perHts` object, you can pass specification parameters that will be applied to the aggregate series. With `iterate = TRUE` (the default), these parameters are also applied to all components recursively:

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Create hierarchical object with custom parameters applied to all nodes
hts_custom <- perHts(
  a = perX13(AirPassengers),
  b = perTramo(AirPassengers),
  template = "rsa1",
  automdl.enabled = FALSE
)

hts_custom$run()
hts_custom
```

The `automdl.enabled = FALSE` setting was applied to both the aggregate series and both components (`a` and `b`). You can verify this by inspecting the specifications:

```{r}
# Check aggregate spec
hts_custom$paramsDirect$automdl.enabled

# Check component a spec
hts_custom$components$a$paramsDirect$automdl.enabled

# Check component b spec
hts_custom$components$b$paramsDirect$automdl.enabled
```

To modify individual components after creation, access them directly:

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Re-enable automdl for component a only
hts_custom$components$a$updateParams(automdl.enabled = TRUE)
hts_custom$components$a$paramsDirect$automdl.enabled
```
